Recueil is a self-hosted server that gathers documents from anywhere — browser, mail, scanner,
WebDAV, camera — keeps a content-addressed library with a bibliographic facet, verifies and
enriches references against the open scholarly graph, and exposes the whole library to R, Python
and LLMs as data. Systematic reviews and bibliometric mapping are native workflows, not exports.

::: {.callout-important}
## Status: Phases 1 and 2 in the tree. No release.

There is no tag, no Docker image and no binary. From a source checkout, `pnpm install && pnpm -r
build` produces a working server, CLI and web client, and the library, the REST contract, the Zotero
and Paperless-ngx migrators, the ingestion pipeline and the three storage backends all run — see
[Getting started](getting-started.qmd) for the tested list and
[the README](https://github.com/etabli-dev/etabli-recueil/blob/main/README.md) for what was measured.

Everything from Phase 3 onwards — enrichment, the checks engine, deduplication, the graph, the
systematic-review module, the desktop and mobile shells, the MCP server — is still a **contract to
be implemented**. Each page marks which roadmap phase brings its subject into existence, and a
command belonging to a later phase says so and exits non-zero rather than half-working.

Neither **M1** (Zotero replaced) nor **M2** (Paperless replaced) is claimed: both ask for the
author's real library and real hardware, and both have so far only been proved against the fixture
corpora in the repository.

Much of this site was written before the code, on purpose: writing the manual first is a cheap way
to find out that a design is unpleasant to explain. Pages that are still ahead of the code say so at
the top.
:::

## What it is meant to be

|  | |
|---|---|
| **Gather** | One ingestion pipeline behind every source: watched folders, WebDAV, IMAP, scanner, mobile capture, the Zotero connector protocol, bulk importers. Files are identified by their SHA-256, never by their path or name. |
| **Verify** | A checks engine that asks whether a reference exists, resolves, has been retracted, has a published version, or contradicts its own metadata. It runs on the library and on reference lists pasted in from outside it. |
| **Map** | Citation, co-citation, coupling, co-word and co-authorship networks built from OpenAlex, Crossref, Semantic Scholar and your own PDFs, with coverage statistics attached to every map, and a Parquet export that lands in R and Python as tables. |
| **Review** | PRISMA 2020 as a first-class workflow: search runs, dedup with per-source tracking, screening, extraction forms, risk of bias, live flow counts. |

It is one AGPL server with thin clients. Zotero's capture ecosystem, Paperless-ngx's ingestion
model, bibliometrix and VOSviewer's analysis layer, and Covidence and Rayyan's screening workflow,
in one place that you run yourself.

## The principles that decide arguments

Ten binding principles run through the whole design; these four come up most often when reading the
rest of the site.

- **The server is the source of truth.** Clients are thin. There is no per-device sync engine, and
  conflicts are logged rather than merged.
- **Content hash is identity.** Files are deduplicated by SHA-256. Path, name and modification time
  never define sameness.
- **Flag, never guess.** An ambiguous ingestion, dedup or enrichment outcome goes to a review queue
  with a logged reason. It is not resolved silently.
- **API-first.** The OpenAPI specification is the contract. The web UI, CLI, MCP server and the R
  and Python packages are all clients of the same API.

The full list of ten is in [CONCEPT.md §3](https://github.com/etabli-dev/etabli-recueil/blob/main/CONCEPT.md).

## Licence and citation

Recueil is licensed under **AGPL-3.0-or-later**. That choice is not incidental: reusing Zotero's
translators and translation-server requires it, and it prevents a hosted fork that gives nothing
back ([ADR-0005](adr.qmd)).

A `CITATION.cff` file is in the repository root, and a Zenodo DOI will be minted at the first
release.
